title: Code Driven Planning with Domain-Adaptive Selector
claim: Prior planners query the LLM repeatedly to replan from short-term feedback; ours uses multiple programs plus a learned critic to cut queries.
layout: 2 panels, left-vs-right, dashed borders, gray caption banners, feedback loops
description: Two side-by-side panels separated by a dashed line. The left panel, 'Other planning: High Querying Cost', shows an LLM logo producing a stack of Plan 1, Plan 2, ..., Plan N speech bubbles. These are executed in a globe icon (the environment) through a large curved 'Execution' arrow. A column of observations marked with red crosses and a final green check comes back, and a curved 'Replan' arrow returns to the LLM. The right panel, 'CoPiC (Ours): Domain Adaption & Reducing Querying Cost', shows an LLM logo above a box titled 'MoE: Planning Programs' with three program icons. These produce Plan 1-3, which a 'Domain-Adaptive Critic' (a doctor icon) marks with two red crosses and one green check. The selected plan goes to the environment, and results and reward arrows loop back through 'Replan' and 'Reinforcement Learning'. Blue and green text highlight the ours-specific elements.
caption: Difference between CoPiC and other planning paradigms: CoPiC leverages multiple high-level planning programs to reduce LLMs query costs, while a domain-adaptive critic is employed to select high-quality plans aligned with long-term rewards.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely adopted as task planners for AI agents in sequential decision-making problems, leveraging their extensive world knowledge. However, the gap between their general knowledge and environment-specific requirements often leads to inaccurate plans. To address this, existing approaches rely on frequent LLM queries to iteratively refine plans based on immediate environmental feedback, which incurs substantial query costs. However, this refinement is typically guided by short-term environmental feedback, limiting LLMs from developing plans aligned with long-term rewards. We propose Co de Driven P lanning w i th Domain-Adaptive Sele C tor (CoPiC). Instead of relying on frequent queries, CoPiC employs LLMs to generate a diverse set of high-level planning programs, which iteratively produce and refine candidate plans. A trained domain-adaptive selector then evaluates these candidates and selects the one most aligned with long-term rewards for execution. Using high-level planning programs as planner and domain-adaptive selector as estimator, CoPiC improves planning while significantly reducing query costs. Results in ALFWorld, NetHack, and StarCraft II Unit Building show that CoPiC outperforms advanced LLM-based baselines, achieving an average (1) 19.14\% improvement in success rate and (2) 79.39\% reduction in token costs.
